Sequence space and the limits of a similarity threshold

Where the phylogeny shows descent, this page shows distance: which types are separable by sequence identity and which are not. It begins with the calibration that matters most, the identities between the characterised enzymes themselves.

1 · Why no single identity cut-off defines a function

Each row is a pair of curated reference enzymes with their experimentally determined substrates. Pairs with different substrates reach the top of the identity range, and pairs sharing a substrate reach far down it, because substrate selection in this family is set by a handful of active-site residues rather than by overall sequence.

2 · Similarity network

Nodes are the references, outlined and enlarged and labelled with the type name, together with one representative per variant, under the same rule as the tree: singletons and variants of 5 or more members are represented, the 604 variants with two to four members are not, which leaves 14 % of entries without a node here. Two nodes are joined when they are at least 35.0 % identical over at least 70 % of their length. Drag the background to pan, scroll to zoom, drag a node to pull a component apart, and click a node to open it. Labels keep a constant size as you zoom, so a crowded region becomes readable by zooming into it.

   

3 · Type against type

ROAR-DB, the Rieske Oxygenase Annotation Resource. Built from RefSeq and GenBank annotation with profile models of 71 Rieske oxygenases characterised in the literature. Every figure states its method and its limits; what the database cannot tell you is documented alongside what it can.
